title: What Happens in Your Body in One Second?
lines: What happens inside your body in a single second?
Start the clock. | The strangest part comes last.
In that second, your heart beats about once.
Each beat pushes out about {70 milliliters~seventy milliliters} of blood.
Your fastest nerve {signals/~signals} travel at up {to/~to} {120 meters~a hundred and twenty meters} per second.
Fast enough to cross a soccer field | in under {1 second.~one second.}
Now dive into a blood vessel. | It's crowded {with/~with} red blood cells.
You have about {25 trillion~twenty-five trillion} of them, | most of the cells in your body.
Each one laps your whole body in about a minute.
To replace them, your bone marrow never stops.
It makes {2 to 3 million/~two to three million} red cells, | every single second.
Each one lives about {120 days,~a hundred and twenty days,} | then it's recycled.
Zoom back out. | Every few seconds, you breathe {in/~in} about half a liter of air.
And your body runs on about {100 watts,~a hundred watts,} | like a bright old light bulb.
Now, the strangest part.
Every day, you replace {roughly/~roughly} {330 billion/~three hundred thirty billion} of your own cells.
That's about {1%~one percent} of you, | almost {4 million~four million} cells every second.
Mostly blood and gut. | In about {3 months,~three months,} most of your blood is new.
By the end of {this/~this} video, | you're not quite the {same/~same} person who started it.
How many times will your heart beat in a lifetime? | About {3 million,~three million,} | or about {3 billion?~three billion?} | Tell me in the comments.

preroll.line: Right now, your body is replacing almost {4 million~four million} cells, every second.
